The Sub-Inspector of Police, Chennammanakere Achukattu Police Station, Bangalore has filed this chargesheet against the Prashanth.S.Sutar vs B.Ananda Reddy on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135604038/
1 accused for the offences punishable U/s.420 of IPC.
 2.The criminal law has been set into motion based on the first information statement of SUBHASH SUTAR..

The gist of the prosecution case is that the accused has opened an office at BSK 3rd stage, Bhuvaneshwari nagar, near Appollo Convent under the name and style Vaibhava Shelters Builders Developers and Promoter office and obtained a Joint Venture to built a building in the Site of CW-2 situated at Sy.No. 61, 64, 65, 66, Kengeri hobili,
Pantharapalya in 25 guntas of land.

It is further alleged that the accused entered into an agreement on 21-03-2013 with CW1 and assured him to give 3 flats for sum of Rs.75,00,000/- and collected cheque for sum of Rs.50 lakhs and received cash of Rs.25 lakhs,
and the accused failed to construct flat in the site of CW-1 and also failed to return the amount to CW-1 and thus cheated CW-1.
Based on the said first information of SUBHASH SUTAR, a case in Crime  3  C.C.No.403/2015 No.109/2013 came to be registered against the Accused for the offences punishable U/s.420 of IPC.
3. Accused was enlarged on bail.
After completion of the investigation, the Police-Sub-Inspector, C.K.Achukattu Police Station, Bangalore has filed this charge sheet against the Accused for the offence punishable U/s.420 of IPC.

On receipt of charge sheet, this court took the cognizance of the alleged offence and the prosecution papers was provided to the accused as required U/s.207 of Cr.P.C.
 4.

Before framing charge, an opportunity of being heard was Prashanth.S.Sutar vs B.Ananda Reddy on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135604038/
2 provided to the accused and after hearing him and the prosecution and as there was sufficient materials, the charge for the aforesaid offence was framed and same was read over to the accused in the language known to him, to which, the accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.
Thereafter, the matter was set down for prosecution evidence.
5. In order to prove the charges, the prosecution has examined PW1 to PW3 witnesses and got marked Ex.P1 to P3 documents.
The Statement of Accused as required U/s. 313 of Cr.P.C., was recorded.
The accused denied the incriminating  4  C.C.No.403/2015 circumstances appearing against him.
The accused has not let in any oral or documentary evidence on his behalf.
6. Heard arguments on both sides.
I have Perused the materials on record.

7. The following point arise for my determination :-
 1) Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable  doubt that the accused entered into an agreement on  21-03-2013 with CW1 and assured him to give 3 flats for  sum of Rs.75,00,000/- and collected cheque for sum of  Rs.50 lakhs and received cash of Rs.25 lakhs, and the  accused failed to construct flat in the site of CW-1 and  also failed to return the amount to CW-1 and thereby the  accused has committed the offence punishable u/s. 420  of IPC.?
 2)
What Order?

8. My finding to the above points are as under:-
 Point No.1.......In the Negative.
 Point No.2.......As per final Order, for the following :-
 REASONS 9. POINT No.1:-

It is the fundamental principle of criminal Prashanth.S.Sutar vs B.Ananda Reddy on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135604038/
3 jurisprudence that the prosecution will have to establish its case beyond all reasonable doubt.

sentences.text: In order to prove the same, the prosecution has examined three witnesses as PW1 to 3 and got marked Ex.P.1 to Ex.P3 documents.
5  C.C.No.403/2015 10. CW-7 was examined as PW-1.
She deposed in her examination in chief that police requested her to give statement of account pertaining to Radhamma.

As per requisition of police, she gave S.B.Account statement pertaining to Radhamma to police as per Ex.P.1.
11. CW-3
was examined as PW-2.
He has deposed in his examination in chief that CW2 is his wife and she is the owner of Sy.No. 61, 64, 65 and 66 measuring 25 guntas situated in Pantarapalya.
He has deposed that in the said land he and the accused had agreed to construct flats under joint venture.
As per the agreement accused paid Rs.10 lakhs and assured to complete the construction within 2 years.
He had also agreed that he would hand over 50% of the constructed flats to them.
However, even after expiry of the period the accused had not completed any work.
When he called upon the accused to get the agreement canceled the accused requested for extension of agreement for a further period of 1 year.
Later again they entered into another agreement and as per the agreement he had received in all 13,40,000/-.
Even after this the accused did not complete any work.
Later the police called him to the station and then he came to know that the accused had  6  C.C.No.403/2015 taken Rs.75,00,000/- from some one and cheated them.

Though Prashanth.S.Sutar vs B.Ananda Reddy on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135604038/
4
the witness was summoned and NBW and proclamation was issued but, he was not secured.
Hence, this court was constrained to drop the witness.
The PW2 had never offered himself for cross examination.
Hence, the entire evidence of PW2 cannot be relied.
12. CW8 was examined as PW3.
He has only deposed regarding producing the accused before the I.O.
13. This being the evidence on record, there is nothing on record to prove the guilt of the accused.
The prosecution has failed to examine the CW1 himself.
When the CW1 who was allegedly cheated is not examined before the court, then no amount of evidence can be held to be sufficient to convict the accused.
Further the evidence of PW2 became unreliable due to him not offering himself for cross examination.
Further the PW2 never came to court stating any cheating from the accused.
The allegations made by the PW2 are only civil in nature in respect of breach of contract.
That cannot be construed as any criminal offence.

Hence,
this court holds that prosecution has failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt.
7  C.C.No.403/2015  Accordingly I answer point No.1 in the Negative.

14. POINT No.2:- In the result, I proceed to pass the following:-
 ORDER
In exercise of power conferred U/s.248(1) of Cr.P.C., accused is acquitted of the offence punishable U/s.420 of IPC.
The bail bond and surety bonds executed by the accused shall remain in force for 6 months.
